verdict.rationale: The official docs say Claude Code follows the Unix philosophy: you can pipe logs into it, run it in CI, or chain it with other tools. They also document CI automation through GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD and scheduled runs, and the auth docs separate interactive from non-interactive key handling. Together these show scripted, non-interactive use as a first-party capability. Missing for 10: documentation of the non-interactive invocation syntax (e.g. a print/headless flag), structured machine-readable output options, and independent hands-on corroboration of scripted use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent non-interactively in scripts for workflow automation

citations.quote: Claude Code is composable and follows the Unix philosophy. Pipe logs into it, run it in CI, or chain it with other tools
In CI, you can automate code review and issue triage with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD.
Run Claude on a schedule to automate work that repeats
